# 2 Maccabees Chapter 10 — The EMET Bible (Literal)

**Translator:** EMET | **Source:** Codex Alexandrinus, 2 Maccabees 10 | **Source Image:** source-texts/greek-DC/2MA_010_page_001.jpg

---

**10:1** Now Maccabeus and his companions, with the Lord leading the way, recovered the temple and the city.

**10:2** And the altars that had been built by foreigners in the public square and also the sacred enclosures they tore down.

**10:3** And having purified the sanctuary, they made another altar; and striking fire from flints, they offered sacrifices after two years' time and incense and lights and the presentation of the bread.

**10:4** Having done this, they fell prostrate and begged the Lord that they might no longer fall into such evils, but that, if ever they should sin, they might be chastened by him with forbearance and not be delivered over to blasphemous and barbarous nations.

**10:5** Now on the very same day on which the sanctuary had been profaned by foreigners, that is, on the twenty-fifth of the same month, which is Chislev, the purification of the temple came about.

**10:6** And they observed eight days with gladness, in the manner of the Feast of Tabernacles, remembering that a short time before, during the Feast of Tabernacles, they had been wandering in the mountains and in caves after the manner of wild beasts.

**10:7** Therefore, bearing ivy-wreathed wands and beautiful branches and also palm fronds, they offered hymns of thanksgiving to him who had successfully brought about the purification of his own place.

**10:8** And they ordained by public decree, with ratification by vote, for the whole nation of the Jews that these days should be observed every year.

**10:9** Such then was the end of Antiochus called Epiphanes.

**10:10** Now we shall set forth the events concerning Antiochus Eupator, the son of the impious man, summarizing the evils that accumulated in the wars.

**10:11** For this man, when he took over the kingdom, appointed one Lysias over the affairs of the realm, and Lysias was appointed commander-in-chief of Coele-Syria and Phoenicia.

**10:12** For Ptolemy, who was called Macron, taking the lead in treating the Jews fairly because of the injustice that had been done to them, attempted to maintain peaceful relations with them.

**10:13** As a result he was accused before Eupator by his friends, and on every side he heard himself called "traitor," because he had abandoned Cyprus, which Philometor had entrusted to him, and had gone over to Antiochus Epiphanes. Since he had no honorable way out of his situation, he ended his life by poison.

**10:14** But Gorgias, who was general of that region, maintained foreign troops and seized every opportunity to make war upon the Jews.

**10:15** Alongside him the Idumeans, holding certain important strongholds, were harassing the Jews. Having welcomed those who had been expelled from Jerusalem, they undertook to keep the war going.

**10:16** And Maccabeus and his men, having made supplication and begged God to be their ally, rushed against the strongholds of the Idumeans.

**10:17** Attacking them vigorously, they gained possession of the positions and repulsed all who fought upon the walls, and those whom they found, they slaughtered; they killed no fewer than twenty thousand.

**10:18** And no fewer than nine thousand fled into two very strong towers well supplied with provisions to withstand a siege.

**10:19** And Maccabeus left Simon and Joseph, and Zacchaeus also and those with him, in sufficient numbers to besiege them, and went away himself to places that were more urgently in need.

**10:20** But those with Simon, being money-lovers, were persuaded by some of those in the towers and having received seventy thousand drachmas let some of them escape.

**10:21** But when it was reported to Maccabeus what had been done, he gathered the leaders of the people and accused those men, that they had sold their kinsmen for silver by releasing their enemies against them.

**10:22** So he put these traitors to death and immediately seized the two towers.

**10:23** And having prospered in everything with his weapons, he destroyed more than twenty thousand in the two strongholds.

**10:24** Now Timothy, who had already been defeated by the Jews, having mustered an exceedingly great multitude of foreign troops, and having brought together much cavalry from Asia, arrived as though to take Judea by spear.

**10:25** As he drew near, Maccabeus and his men sprinkled earth upon their heads and girded their loins with sackcloth, falling on the step of the altar and begging him to be gracious to them and to be an enemy to their enemies and an adversary to their adversaries, as the law declares.

**10:26** And having prayed in this manner, taking up their weapons, they advanced a considerable distance from the city, and when they drew near to the enemies they halted.

**10:27** But just as the dawn was breaking, the two forces joined battle. The one party had, as pledge of success and victory, not only their valor but also the retreat to the Lord as their refuge; the other took their rage as guide in the battle.

**10:28** When the battle became fierce, there appeared to the enemies from heaven five resplendent men on horses with golden bridles, who placed themselves at the head of the Jews

**10:29** and surrounding Maccabeus with themselves, and covering him with their own armor, kept him unharmed, while hurling arrows and thunderbolts upon the enemies, so that, confused and blinded, they were disorganized and overwhelmed with confusion.

**10:30** Twenty thousand five hundred were slain, along with six hundred horsemen.

**10:31** Timothy himself fled to a stronghold called Gazara, very strong, with Chaereas in command.

**10:32** But Maccabeus and his men rejoiced and besieged the fortress for four days.

**10:33** And those within, trusting in the strength of the place, blasphemed exceedingly and hurled abominable words.

**10:34** But when the fifth day dawned, twenty young men of Maccabeus's company, inflamed with anger because of the blasphemies, rushed the wall with manly courage and with savage fury cut down everyone they came upon.

**10:35** Others who had come up similarly, while the besieged were occupied with attacking those men, set fire to the towers and kindled fires and burned the blasphemers alive; still others broke open the gates, and having admitted the rest of the force, they occupied the first courts.

**10:36** And Timothy hid himself in a pit. But they found him and killed him, along with his brother Chaereas and Apollophanes.

**10:37** When these things had been accomplished, they praised the Lord with hymns and thanksgiving, him who does great benefits for Israel and gives them the victory.

**10:38** After a little while, Lysias the king's guardian and kinsman and administrator of the affairs of state came to Judea with a great force.
